Oom Frans and his newspapers : News of the Hantam

By: Anina Peens | Commission

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Thought it was the end of the print paper? This news has not reached Frans Hugo in the heart of the Karoo.

Unique Selling Point:
A heart for news and telling stories is what keeps this 92 year journalist and his three weekly newspapers alive!

Summary:
While the future of print news hangs in the balance and the journalistic profession is abound with uncertainty, 90 year old journalist, Frans Hugo from Calvinia seems unaffected.
In his small newsroom on the main street of the small town in the heart of the Hantam Karoo, Frans produces three weekly newspapers; ‘The Messenger’, ‘Die Noordwester’ and ‘Die Owernuus’. And then, every Thursday morning he leaves his home at 1:30 in the morning to deliver the newspapers across the region, driving over 1200km and returning to Calvinia on the same day.




Further information:
He doesn't know when it's going to end, all he knows is, he can't stop now. He wil stop when he stops and that will probably be when he dies. Until then, he does everyday, what he does best and that is working on his three community news papers in the heart of the arid Karoo.

In a small town in the Hantam Karoo, Frans Hugo and his wife move into their newsroom, Die Noordwester, every Sunday afternoon. Frans goes to sit at his computer looking for fresh stories for the week ahead, while his wife makes them something to eat. Every week, Frans says, he hopes that the advertisers will return and that he will have enough news by Wednesday to print his paper deep into the nightly hours of Thursday morning. He lays out the paper together with his wife at two o clock in the morning. Then, when the staff arrives around 6am, the printing starts on old fashioned machines that are not even in use anymore.

At one o clock in the morning, every Thursday, Frans packs the piles of the newspaper in his car and drives 1200km across the region to hand deliver his paper to surrounding towns. This while one of his three staff members rides an old fashioned bicycle to deliver the paper in Calviinia town.

This story is truly a walk back in time to a bygone area where newspapers are printed like they used to be more than 30 years ago.

NEWS OF THE HANTAM: VIEWING 1

OPENING
VO
It’s a strenuous news cycle that starts every Sunday,

… and 91-year-old journalist Frans Hugo has no time to waste if he’s to make his Thursday deadline.

UPSOUND: MUSIC
FOOTAGE: DELIVERY MAN ON BICYCLE

VO
Far from the trappings of a mainstream newsroom, this is a newsroom in the main street of small-town Karoo. A place called Calvinia, in the Hantam district.

SUPER@ ERWIN COETZEE
TIM: CLIP 0119
06:02:09:46
Hy is so deel van Calvinia soos die rooi posbus wat hier oorkant hom staan…

VO
With printed newspapers on the decline globally, Frans and his team are bucking the trend.

SUPER@ FRANS HUGO
SOURCE: TIM
CLIP 0019
00:25:51:00
Of its dying, people don’t read newspapers anymore. And now Im just, I don’t know when to stop it…


FADE TO BLACK


PART 1

VO
The Noordwester’s newsroom appears preserved in a time capsule,
…a window into a bygone era.

UPSOUND: PRINT MACHINES

VO
Frans Hugo has been producing three different community newspapers every week for the past 45 years.

LINK
CLIP: 0062
Walking through here is like taking a step back into history… I mean I can’t imagine what’s it must’ve been like, all of these years ago, trying to print a newspaper. In Calvinia, it still happens that way. I mean look at this.

VO
Frans got his start in papers as what’s known as a “letterpress”, later becoming the editor of a publication in Namibia. After a stint at Die Burger in Cape Town he bought the Noordewester in 1979.

SUPER@ FRANS HUGO
SOURCE: TIM
CLIP 0019
00:29:20:18
I bought a linotype. Do you know linotype? That’s a led machine…
SUPER@ FRANS HUGO
SOURCE: TIM
CLIP 0019
00:38:10:13
I am not a natural typist, it’s a work for me to type, but you can’t get away from that. When I had a linotype, it was a different keyboard, and I could work that quite well.

SUPER@ FRANS HUGO
SOURCE: TIM
CLIP 0019
00:29:20:18
and then we carried on with that and then we started with a phototypesetting, so I went over the USA and I bought one of those things over there. It was a problem to learn how to work with it. But then we eventually got over to the computer.

SUPER@ FRANS HUGO
SOURCE: TIM
CLIP 0019
00:38:10:13
I should be able to type after all these years, with two fingers.

VO
Frans’s 80-year-old wife, Maxi Hugo, is co-editor. She’s grown accustomed to the late nights and early mornings her husband has been keeping for nearly half a century.

SUPER@ FRANS HUGO
SOURCE: TIM
CLIP 0019
00:39:13:33
We don’t live here, we just sleep over here for three days to make a newspaper. Otherwise, we live at our house on the other side of town.

VO
Frans writes all of the week’s stories and, once they’re finalised, he and Maxi are up at 3am every Wednesday to work on the paper’s layout.

The printing presses can’t be kept waiting.

UPSOUND: STAFF WORKING
Privileged
SUPER@ MARTHA VAN WYK
CLIP 0067
05:33:06:05
MAC: 1981?
5 March ja..
MAC: I was only one years old… I was only one years old!
Toe is ek 19 jaar oud toe ek hier begin werk het.
MAC: Tot nou.
Nee, ek was 61 was, toe is nou vir ‘n jaar en vyf maande by die huis, toe het ek nou Junie maand weer begin
MAC: toe kom jy maar terug
Martha: toe kom ek maar weer terug.

VO
Martha van Wyk is one of four staff members who’ve all committed a lifetime to the newspaper.

SUPER@ MARTHA VAN WYK
CLIP 0067
05:34:55:25
Hier het baie baie mense gewerk in my leeftyd in. Wat nou weer ander weivelde gaan soek het, beter werk gekry het en beter verdien het, maar ek dink baie van die goed het hulle hier geleer, dan is hulle nou hier weg.

VO
For Martha, Frans’ newsroom has cultivated a love of reading and sharing information

SUPER@ MARTHA VAN WYK
CLIP 0067
05:33:54:45
Ek dink die koerant bring nuus wat baie van ons mense nie ken nie. Ek is mal oor lees.
CLIP 0062
01:18:26:43
Elke dag is interessant by ons en elke dag of elke week kry ons ‘n koerant waarna ons uitsien.

VO
Here in the Hantam, seeing the faces of people you know in a newspaper is worth more than likes and shares online.

SUPER@ FRANS HUGO
SOURCE: TIM
CLIP 0062
01:19:32:47
Daar is niks lekkerder as om jou foto in die koerant te sien nie. Facebook of sosiale media is nou al so vervelig. Dis maar net ‘n gewone foto en more was jy dit af, of jy vee dit uit, onmiddelik, maar ‘n koerantfoto sal daar bly.

VO
It’s one of the reasons the paper has survived.

SUPER@ FRANS HUGO
SOURCE: TIM
CLIP 0019
00:34:14:22
They like their own picture in there, even if its just in black and white in my newspaper. That’s one of the reasons why I think the newspaper situation is collapsing, full colored pictures, full staff. Over here we just do it ourselves.

VO
Mounting costs in the print media have coincided with declining readerships. Die Burger, where Frans once worked, reportedly dwindled from about 60 thousand in 2014 to 27 thousand in 2022.

PAUSE

VO
The Noordewester, meanwhile, stays afloat with money from advertising.

SUPER@ FRANS HUGO
SOURCE: TIM
CLIP 0019
00:40:39:40
We are lucky to have every week a full color advert, from Spar which pays the wages every week. So, all I have to do is make enough money from the municipality and the rest of the traveling and what have you.

VO
And, almost miraculously, come Wednesday, there are enough ads and stories to compile a paper.

TIM: 0044
01:01:57:30
Ek het mos nou my boeke hierso wat ek kan opskrywe, advertensies en stories wat ek gekry het, en fotos.

VO
From Sunday to Wednesday, Frans patiently waits for stories to be emailed so he can write the articles.

SUPER@ ERWIN COETZEE
TIM: CLIP 0119
05:59:30:47
Ek dink dit is die laaste van ‘n era. Daar sal nie weer so iemand wees nie.

VO
For locals like Dr Erwin Coetzee, the newspaper has become an institution in the community.

SUPER@ ERWIN COETZEE
TIM: CLIP 0119
05:58:56:19
Die papier wat jy voel, Frans se taalgebruik, is pragtig, jy lees dit Afrikaans en dit het alles betrekking tot dit hier om jou.
SUPER@ ERWIN COETZEE
TIM: CLIP 0119
05:58:27:49
Dit is die spilpunt van ons gemeenskap, dis bevat alles wat ons gemeenskap met ingelig word oor en wat betrekking het tot osn gemeenskap. Ek meen jy kan die tv nuus kyk maar dit gee vir jou wat in Israel gebeur. Die Noordwester sê vir jou wat hier in Calvina gebeur.

VO
But stories are sent from across the region to feature in all three newspapers.

UPSOUNDS:
TIM: 0046
Loxton se kerk is nou 100 jaar ouden daai mense het nou ‘n advertensie by my geplaas, nou met ek maar begin om dit ‘n koerantstorie te maak. [JW1]

VO
In town, the papers are sold and delivered by bicycle.

SUPER@ FRANS HUGO
SOURCE: TIM
CLIP 0019
00:26:10:42
They pay R8 for this little newspaper.
MAC: Eight Rand?
Ja, R8 in nowadays you can buy a box of matches as well.

VO
But the bike can only cover a small area. To ensure a healthy circulation, Frans hand delivers to towns across the region.


SUPER@ FRANS HUGO
SOURCE: TIM
CLIP 0019
00:32:39:19
I wake up one o clock and then I start driving half past, or two o clock.
00:37:00:49
My wife puts in a lot of food for me. Kaas en brood en deesdae vat ek nou biltong en droeewors.

VO
Every Thursday, from one in the morning until seven at night, Frans travels over 1200 kilometres.

GRAPHIC
CALVINA- WILLISTON-CARNAVON-VOSBURG-BRITSTOWN-PRIESKA-BRITSTOWN-VICTORIA WEST- LOXTON-CARNAVON-CALVINIA

SIT DIE BYTE OOR DIE GRAPHIC
SUPER@ FRANS HUGO
SOURCE: TIM
CLIP 0019
00:31:53:26
There is no other way to get it there. Train is not working. I used a train when I started here. and of course, the post office is now closed down. So there is no other way I can get it over there.

VO
But there’s little time to rest on his return. He spends Fridays and Saturdays balancing the books before the cycle starts again on a Sunday.

PART 3

[JW2]




UPSOUND: GAMMIE WAT MENSE STOP IN STRAAT

VO
Traffic officer Jan Isaacs, known as Gammie has been a loyal reader for over 30 years.

SUPER@ JAN ISAACS (GAMMIE)
CLIP: 0116
05:53:11:23
Daar is sekere baie belangrike dinge of aspekte wat binne die gemeenskap plaasvind wat mense nie van weet nie, en dan koop die mense die koerantjie en dan sien die mense dit. Misdywe wat gepleeg word binne ons gemeenskappe, die koerant dra by, gesteelde goedere wat deur die polisie gesoek word is ook ‘n goeie bydrae

VO
Seeing his own picture in the newspaper spurred him on as a youngster.

SUPER@ JAN ISAACS (GAMMIE)
CLIP: 0116
05:51:08:25
Ons is regtigwaar bevoorregt om die Noordwester by ons te he. Toe ek in Calvinia kom het ek die pragtige koerantjie hier gekry, dieNoordwester. Ek het in Calvinia gekom as ‘n baie goeie atleet en dit is die einste koerant wat my op die map gesit het. Ek het verskillende maratonne gewen… en hierdie koerant het my naam sommer goed opgelig.

VO
Social media, Gammie says, just isn’t the same.

SUPER@ JAN ISAACS (GAMMIE)
CLIP: 0116
05:55:04:14
Die enigste bleikie waardering wat ons vir oom Frans en sy wonderlike vrou kan gee vir hierdie deursettingsvermoe, is om elke Donderdag sy koerant te koop.

LINK
CLIP: 0080
If there’s anything that oom Frans can teach us all is that despite your age if you love what you do and you do what you love, that passion will keep you alive and I guess age is then, just a number.

SUPER@ FRANS HUGO
SOURCE: TIM
CLIP 0019
00:48:17:30
I’m lucky to be able to still work. Most people at 80 they sit at home, and six months later they burry them or burn them, I am lucky to have lived 20 years longer than what I should have lived.

SHOT OF HIM WALKING DOWN THE PASSAGE

TIMELINE PROMOS

PROMO 1
VO
When passion does it, age is just a number.
SUPER@ FRANS HUGO
SOURCE: TIM
CLIP 0019
00:24:41:12
“I talked to an old friend the other day and he asked how old are you and I said, 91 and he said, you’re going for a 100 now!
VO
Not even old age can deter journalist Frans Hugo from publishing three newspapers every week from deep in the Karoo.
SUPER@ ERWIN COETZEE
TIM: CLIP 0119
05:59:30:47
Ek dink dit is die laaste van ‘n era. Daar sal nie weer so iemand wees nie.

PROMO 2
For a small town in the Karoo, a weekly newspaper is the backbone of their community.
SUPER@ JAN ISAACS (GAMMIE)
CLIP: 0116
05:52:51:27
Ek koop hom elke week, ek kannie wag dat dit Donderdag moet raak nie, want ek moet seker maar dat ek daai storietjies opvang.
VO
But even more so, the 91 year old journalist who publishes it every week.
SUPER@ ERWIN COETZEE
TIM: CLIP 0119
06:01:51:32
Almal lees oor oom Frans, se berigte, hy beïnvloed tog ons dorp, en hy gee ons dorp iets om oor te praat. Ons is trots op oom Frans.

PROMO 3
VO
As the printing press is on a decline, it's not stopping this 91 year old journalist.
SUPER@ FRANS HUGO
SOURCE: TIM
CLIP 0019
00:47:36:12
If journalism disappears, the government will do what they like without being criticised.
VO
From the Karoo, Frans Hugo prints and hand delivers his newspapers to an entire region, every week.
SUPER@ ERWIN COETZEE
TIM: CLIP 0119
05:59:58:48
Daar kannie weer so joernalis wees wat elke week sy koerant gaan versprei…1200 kilometer ry met ‘n kar wat gereeld breek, en dan maak hy hom reg… dan gaan versprei hy sy koerant.




[JW1]Dr could come in here. Would fit nicely.
[JW2]This is what would move up.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Thought it was the end of the print paper? This news has not reached Frans Hugo in the heart of the Karoo.
metadata.Unique Selling Point: A heart for news and telling stories is what keeps this 92 year journalist and his three weekly newspapers alive!
metadata.Summary: While the future of print news hangs in the balance and the journalistic profession is abound with uncertainty, 90 year old journalist, Frans Hugo from Calvinia seems unaffected. In his small newsroom on the main street of the small town in the heart of the Hantam Karoo, Frans produces three weekly newspapers; ‘The Messenger’, ‘Die Noordwester’ and ‘Die Owernuus’. And then, every Thursday morning he leaves his home at 1:30 in the morning to deliver the newspapers across the region, driving over 1200km and returning to Calvinia on the same day.
metadata.Further information: He doesn't know when it's going to end, all he knows is, he can't stop now. He wil stop when he stops and that will probably be when he dies. Until then, he does everyday, what he does best and that is working on his three community news papers in the heart of the arid Karoo. In a small town in the Hantam Karoo, Frans Hugo and his wife move into their newsroom, Die Noordwester, every Sunday afternoon. Frans goes to sit at his computer looking for fresh stories for the week ahead, while his wife makes them something to eat. Every week, Frans says, he hopes that the advertisers will return and that he will have enough news by Wednesday to print his paper deep into the nightly hours of Thursday morning. He lays out the paper together with his wife at two o clock in the morning. Then, when the staff arrives around 6am, the printing starts on old fashioned machines that are not even in use anymore. At one o clock in the morning, every Thursday, Frans packs the piles of the newspaper in his car and drives 1200km across the region to hand deliver his paper to surrounding towns. This while one of his three staff members rides an old fashioned bicycle to deliver the paper in Calviinia town. This story is truly a walk back in time to a bygone area where newspapers are printed like they used to be more than 30 years ago.
